gap: No result ChatGPT got states the measured no-load (idle) draw of the 3,000 Wh candidates side by side, nor any measured usable capacity or switchover for the BLUETTI Elite 300. The Solar Lab measured idle at 8 W (Jackery HomePower 3000), about 15 W (BLUETTI Elite 300), 20.5 W (Anker F3000), about 22 W (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra) and 37 W (Pecron F3000LFP), which is 384 Wh to 1,776 Wh over a two-day outage.
standout_why: Compared against all the cited pages except Good Housekeeping, which could not be fetched. wattpowerstation.com (guide and /power-stations/ index) has tested usable Wh for the Jackery HomePower 3000 (2,759), Anker F3000 (2,613), DELTA 3 Ultra Plus (2,611) and Pecron F3000LFP (2,550), but no idle draw, noise or measured switchover, and no Elite 300 row. powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000 has only maker switchover and weight figures and a 0.85 assumption. thesolarlab.com's big-station roundup gives idle only for the F3800 Plus and Apex 300 and omits the HomePower 3000 and Elite 300. powersized.com, power-verdict.com, thepowerstationreport.com and lightsonlabs.com state they do not test. So the usable-capacity half is already covered for the rivals; the idle-draw table and the Elite 300 measurements (three capacity tests, two switchover tests) are new. One caveat: wattpowerstation's per-model Jackery page, which ChatGPT did not get, says the unit 'used 36.4% of its energy on itself' in a fridge test, which sits awkwardly with an 8 W idle.
decides: It confirms the Jackery HomePower 3000 as the outage pick: lowest measured idle (8 W) on top of 2,759 Wh usable. It moves the BLUETTI Elite 300 ahead of the cheaper Pecron F3000LFP as the value pick for a fridge-through-an-outage use: the Pecron's 37 W idle costs about 1,776 Wh over 48 h against about 720 Wh for the Elite 300, and the Elite 300's measured usable AC energy (2,650 to 2,819 Wh) is at or above the Pecron's 2,550 Wh despite the smaller rating. The Elite 300's switchover measured 8 ms (StorageReview) and 8.9 ms (The Technology Man), under its 10 ms rating, while the 20 ms figures for the Jackery, Anker and Pecron are maker ratings only. The Elite 300's cost is noise: about 50 dB at 1 m under load, against about 35 dB for the Anker F3000.
